reports.title: CleanSpark Reports Fiscal Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2026 Financial and Operating Results

desk.headline: Revenue down 46% to $120.9m, below estimates; small $9.8m profit on bitcoin revaluation gain; no guidance

other.label: Gain on fair value of bitcoin

results: Mining revenue fell 46% to $120.9m, short of the $127.7m estimate, as the fleet shrank and hashrate dropped.
A $305.6m gain on the value of its bitcoin offset a $171.7m impairment, leaving net income of $9.8m ($0.04 a share).
Full year: revenue $576.5m (-25%) and a net loss of $987.1m, driven by bitcoin value losses, higher depreciation and impairments.
Signed a 20-year, $6.6bn triple-net lease at Sandersville, Georgia, funded by $2.276bn of 7.875% secured notes due 2031.
Year-end liquidity about $1.3bn ($204.8m cash plus $1.13bn of bitcoin); long-term debt rose to $3.99bn from $0.64bn.

guidance.summary: CleanSpark gives no financial guidance. It says the first Sandersville data hall is on track for November 2027.

points: CEO Matt Schultz framed the year as a shift from bitcoin mining to data-centre development, anchored by the Sandersville lease.
Exclusivity on the Texas sites (Sealy and Brazoria) lapsed during a state regulatory pause; ERCOT and PUCT meetings in mid-December are the next steps.
CFO Gary Vecchiarelli said there is no need or appetite for equity financing; bitcoin sales or borrowing will fund deals.
No major new mining capex is planned; Sandersville miners are due to be switched off in late 2027.
Spare cash is earmarked for acquisitions rather than share buybacks; no new buyback was announced.

watch: Texas regulatory decisions in December and whether leases follow at Sealy and Brazoria.
Sandersville construction cost and timing against the November 2027 first-hall target.
Bitcoin price swings, which drive large non-cash gains and losses in reported profit.
